phase_b_scope: Steps 1-3 and 5 only. Step 4 (confirmation re-crawl) not run - no database.
status_note: All five steps ran. Suite green, every rule-level difference in the confirmation re-crawl explained, no P1 left unfixed. The Phase A run this fixes remains coverage_complete:false — that is a property of the audit, not of these fixes.

commits.message: fix(findings): mark findings derived from a truncated body [D1]
fix(broken-external-link): retry an external HEAD timeout with GET [D2]
fix(title-multiple): exclude SVG and MathML from document elements [D3]
feat(crawlScope): serve the per-rule findings rollup on /runs/:id/findings [D4]

fixtures_note: Conditions synthesised in-test rather than committed as artifacts: D1 uses a result with bodyTruncated set, not the 14MB page; D2 and D3 use local http servers reproducing the behaviour.

url_sets.verdict: 99.2% overlap - the rule-level diff below is meaningful

explanations.title-multiple: D3. SVG <title> chart labels no longer counted as document titles. Expected exactly 2 -> 0.
explanations.broken-external-link: D2. 1021 -> 4. Predicted ~-966 (two icann.org links at 483 each); actual -1017, so ~51 further instances came from other hosts that also hang on HEAD and answer GET. Larger than predicted, same cause.
explanations.external-403: -4. URL-set churn: the rule fired once per source page for one icann.org footer link, and 4 of those source pages were not reached this run.
explanations.meta-missing: -4. Four fewer HTML pages crawled (/domains/root/db/*.html), one finding each.
explanations.slow-page: 233 -> 119. NOT a code change. The rule fires on responseTime > 1000ms and the re-crawl has exactly 119 internal results over 1000ms. The distribution sits on the threshold (p75 = 999ms), so ordinary latency variance moves ~100 pages across it. This rule cannot serve as a regression signal in a confirmation diff.

d4_measurement.method: curl against GET /runs/<id>/findings on the confirmation re-crawl, 3 samples each, same run, same server, before and after the change.

default_unchanged.note: 19 bytes larger for the new grain field; instance grain is still the default so the report and review flow are unaffected.

d4_measurement.reconciles: 17 rollup rows sum to 6,147 - exactly findingsCount.
d4_measurement.correction: findings.md and deferred.md cited 2,083,798 bytes / 9.80s as Phase A's numbers. Those were the books.toscrape run (1,694 findings), not iana.org. Per-finding they are consistent (~1.1KB); the attribution was wrong. This is why a before/after must be measured on one run.
